narrative:
Your loan application was reviewed by an automated credit assessment system, which predicted a 51% probability that you represent a bad credit risk — a borderline decision, but one that ultimately resulted in a denial. This means the system assessed your financial profile as slightly more likely to lead to repayment difficulties than not, placing you just on the wrong side of the approval threshold.

To understand what would need to change for your application to be approved, it helps to think in terms of "what if" scenarios — alternative versions of your profile where one or more factors are different enough to tip the prediction in your favor. These scenarios, called counterfactuals, reveal which aspects of your financial situation the model found most concerning and what adjustments could realistically lead to an approval.

In your case, the analysis generated one such scenario, and it points to a single, decisive factor: the status of your checking account. Currently, your checking account is in a negative balance — below 0 Deutsche Marks — and this alone appears to be the primary reason your application was denied. The one scenario that would flip the decision to an approval requires only this one change: moving your checking account to a healthier standing, specifically to a status with no checking account or a positive balance. No other feature in your profile needed to change for the model to reconsider its decision.

This is a remarkably focused finding. Out of 17 features evaluated, 16 of them — including your loan amount of 1,108 DM, your 12-month repayment duration, your employment of 4 to 7 years, your real estate property, and your stable housing situation — were already acceptable to the model and did not need to change at all. Your loan request is actually quite modest compared to the average approved applicant, who typically borrows around 2,887 DM, which works in your favor. Your employment stability and property ownership are also solid positives.

The one area pulling your application down is the negative checking account balance, which signals to the system a current liquidity strain. Among approved applicants, nearly half had either no checking account or a balance of 200 DM or more, while only about 20% had a negative balance like yours. Resolving this — by clearing any overdraft or building a positive balance before reapplying — would be the single most impactful step you could take. Given the otherwise strong profile you present, addressing your checking account status is the clearest and most actionable path toward a successful loan application.
